title: D-Bus: desktop.reloadConfig() from Plasma desktop scripting does not visually update wallpaper until plasmashell is restarted
line: When a script writes a new picture over the image file already used as the wallpaper, the desktop now shows it right away.
explanation: The reporter's script reuses the same file paths (split-0.png, split-1.png) and only changes their content, so the configured Image URL never changes and reloadConfig() has nothing to apply. The image wallpaper watches its file with KDirWatch but only reacted to 'created', which fires when a file is replaced by a new one, not when it is overwritten in place ('dirty'). The change also reloads on 'dirty', and when such a reload hits a half-written file that fails to decode it keeps the current picture instead of falling back to the default wallpaper; the next change event loads the finished file.

commits.message:
wallpapers/image: reload the wallpaper when its file is overwritten

Only newly created files were noticed, so writing new content to the
image already used as wallpaper kept showing the old picture until a
restart. React to in-place changes too, and skip half-written files.

BUG: 506862

media.caption: Master: wallpaper is split-0.png (Kite); after overwriting that file with Altai and running the reporter's currentConfig + reloadConfig() script, Kite is still shown (right).
With the fix: same steps; the wallpaper switches to Altai as soon as the file is overwritten, and stays correct after the script runs (right).

review.text: Good root-cause diagnosis showing the real trigger is overwriting the same wallpaper file path in place rather than reloadConfig() itself. Connecting KDirWatch::dirty in MediaProxy and keeping the current wallpaper on Image.Error during live file updates in ImageStackView.qml is clean, avoids resetting to the default wallpaper during slow non-atomic writes, and keeps normal initial-load error fallback intact. Evidence and regression checks thoroughly prove the fix.
